section: Earth observation - IRS series, Cartosat, Resourcesat, Oceansat, RISAT, EOS series and applications
subsections: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites

accepted.s: The Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) programme was initiated in which year?
accepted.x: The IRS programme began in 1988 and developed into the world's largest civilian remote-sensing constellation.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive programme-start year to eliminate nearby dates.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bhaskara-1 and Bhaskara-2 — experimental precursors to the IRS programme
Cartosat-1 and Cartosat-2 — ocean altimetry satellites
accepted.x: Bhaskara-1 and Bhaskara-2 preceded the operational IRS programme as experimental satellites.
accepted.tq: Match the satellite pair with its distinctive programme role.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the early IRS satellites:
1. IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988.
2. IRS-1B was launched in 1991.
3. IRS-1C was launched in 1995.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: IRS-1A, IRS-1B and IRS-1C were launched in 1988, 1991 and 1995 respectively.
accepted.tq: Check each date independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: IRS-1A, IRS-1B and IRS-1C were launched from Baikonur on Soviet rockets. Which one of the following was the first IRS satellite launched by PSLV from Sriharikota?
accepted.x: IRS-P2 was the first IRS satellite launched on PSLV from Sriharikota; the earlier IRS-1A, 1B and 1C missions used Soviet rockets from Baikonur.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the early Baikonur missions from the first Sriharikota PSLV mission.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the principal application of the Resourcesat series?
o: Natural-resource management, including crop acreage and watershed studies
accepted.x: Resourcesat-1, Resourcesat-2 and Resourcesat-2A are used for natural-resource applications such as crop acreage, watershed studies and precision farming.
accepted.tq: Identify the application from the series name and its resource-oriented function.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Resourcesat satellites are especially associated with which agricultural practice?
accepted.x: Precision farming is one of the stated applications of the Resourcesat series, along with crop-acreage and watershed assessment.
accepted.tq: Select the specific application belonging to the natural-resources series.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cartosat satellites are primarily designed for:
accepted.x: Cartosat-1, Cartosat-2 and Cartosat-3 are high-resolution mapping satellites also used for surveillance.
accepted.tq: Match the satellite series with its dominant operational function.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Cartosat:
1. The Cartosat series provides high-resolution mapping data.
2. Cartosat-3 provides approximately 25-centimetre imagery.
3. Cartosat data can support Smart Cities and Gati Shakti initiatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Cartosat supports high-resolution mapping, Cartosat-3 provides about 25 cm imagery, and its data have applications in Smart Cities, Gati Shakti and border surveillance.
accepted.tq: Combine the resolution figure with the listed planning applications.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Oceansat — ocean colour and sea-surface temperature
accepted.x: HySIS is a hyperspectral-imaging satellite. Direct-to-home broadcasting is associated with communication satellites, not HySIS.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched application by separating EO functions from communication functions.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Oceansat-1 was launched in which year?
accepted.x: Oceansat-1 was launched in 1999; Oceansat-2 and Oceansat-3 followed in the series.
accepted.tq: Use the series-specific launch year rather than the general IRS start year.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories generated from ocean-observation data are most directly useful to:
accepted.x: Oceansat observations support PFZ advisories, which help fishermen identify areas likely to have higher fish availability.
accepted.tq: Translate the technical abbreviation PFZ into its practical user group.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly describes Oceansat observations?
1. Ocean colour
2. Sea-surface temperature
3. Surface wind
4. Potential Fishing Zone advisories
accepted.x: The Oceansat series supports all four listed applications: ocean colour, sea-surface temperature, surface-wind observation and PFZ advisories.
accepted.tq: Recognise the broad application set of an ocean-observation series.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: RISAT satellites use which technology for imaging under cloudy conditions and at night?
accepted.x: RISAT-1, RISAT-2 and RISAT-2B use Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), enabling all-weather, day-and-night imaging through clouds.
accepted.tq: Distinguish radar-based RISAT imaging from optical Earth observation.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following applications is associated with the RISAT series?
1. Flood monitoring
2. Counter-terrorism operations
3. All-weather imaging through clouds
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: RISAT's SAR capability supports flood monitoring, counter-terrorism and day-night, all-weather imaging through clouds.
accepted.tq: Link the SAR capability to its operational applications.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: SCATSAT-1 is equipped with a scatterometer primarily for measuring:
accepted.x: SCATSAT-1 uses a scatterometer to measure ocean-surface wind vectors, supporting cyclone forecasting.
accepted.tq: Match the sensor type with the parameter it measures.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which satellite is associated with hyperspectral imaging?
accepted.x: HySIS is India's hyperspectral-imaging satellite.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive sensor-related name to identify the satellite.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EOS-03, also known as GISAT-1, was intended primarily for:
o: Near-real-time geo-imaging of floods and cyclones
Measuring ocean winds for cyclone forecasting
accepted.x: EOS-03, formerly GISAT-1, was designed for geo-imaging and near-real-time observation of events such as floods and cyclones.
accepted.tq: Separate the intended mission application from the later launch outcome.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EOS-03 was lost during which launch mission?
accepted.x: EOS-03, or GISAT-1, was lost during the GSLV-F10 mission in 2021.
accepted.tq: Match the satellite failure with the correct launch vehicle mission and year.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EOS-04 is also known as:
accepted.x: EOS-04 is the new designation of RISAT-1A and uses SAR for Earth observation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the old and new names of closely related EO satellites.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes EOS-04?
o: A communication satellite placed in geostationary orbit
A scatterometer devoted to ocean wind vectors
An optical satellite used only for ocean-colour studies
A SAR satellite useful for observing crops under cloud cover
accepted.x: EOS-04, formerly RISAT-1A, is a SAR satellite capable of observing crops even under cloud cover; it was also used in the CROP wheat estimate for 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Use the cloud-penetrating SAR capability to identify the correct description.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EOS-06 is the new designation of which satellite?
accepted.x: EOS-06 is also known as Oceansat-3 and supports Potential Fishing Zone advisories.
accepted.tq: Test the renaming relationship within the Oceansat–EOS sequence.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EOS-07, launched on 10 February 2023, was carried by:
accepted.x: EOS-07 was launched on 10 February 2023 by SSLV-D2 as a technology-demonstration mission.
accepted.tq: Match the date, launch vehicle and mission purpose as a single factual unit.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: EOS-08 is best described as:
o: A geosynchronous imager launched on GSLV-F17 in 2026
A microsatellite launched on SSLV-D3 in 2024
An ocean altimetry satellite developed with CNES
A SAR satellite launched on PSLV-C61 in 2025
accepted.x: EOS-08 is a microsatellite launched on SSLV-D3 in 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the EOS-08 technology mission from the other EOS launch profiles.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding EOS-05 is correct?
1. It was formerly known as GISAT-1A.
2. It was launched by GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026.
3. It was the first Earth-observation imager working from geosynchronous orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: EOS-05 was formerly GISAT-1A, was launched on GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026, and became the first EO imager working from geosynchronous orbit.
accepted.tq: Verify the former name, launch details and unique orbital achievement together.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the reported launch failure?
1. EOS-09 — PSLV-C61, May 2025
2. EOS-N1 ‘Anvesha’ — PSLV-C62, January 2026
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: EOS-09, a C-band SAR satellite, failed to reach orbit on PSLV-C61 in May 2025. DRDO's hyperspectral EOS-N1, named Anvesha, failed on PSLV-C62 in January 2026.
accepted.tq: Check each failure against its launch vehicle and date before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: NISAR is a joint Earth-observation mission of:
accepted.x: NISAR is the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar mission.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct international partnership rather than the sensor type alone.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about NISAR:
1. It was launched on 30 July 2025 by GSLV-F16.
2. It is the world's first dual-frequency radar satellite.
3. It uses L-band radar from NASA and S-band radar from ISRO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NISAR was launched on GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025 and carries NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band radars, making it the first dual-frequency radar satellite of its kind.
accepted.tq: Combine mission date, record and agency-wise instrument contribution.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the coverage and antenna features of NISAR?
o: It scans only the oceans every 12 months using a Ka-band altimeter.
It scans India every 3 days using a 1-metre communication antenna.
It scans nearly the whole Earth every 12 days and has a 12-metre antenna reflector deployed in orbit.
It scans the whole Earth every 24 hours using a 25-centimetre optical reflector.
accepted.x: NISAR scans nearly the whole Earth every 12 days and carries a 12-metre antenna reflector deployed in orbit.
accepted.tq: Pair the coverage interval with the distinctive antenna dimension.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: SARAL — hyperspectral imaging of agricultural fields
accepted.x: SARAL is an ISRO-CNES altimetry mission using the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter to measure sea-surface height; hyperspectral agricultural imaging is associated with HySIS.
accepted.tq: Find the single application belonging to another satellite series.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following IRS-related events in chronological order:
A. Launch of IRS-1A
B. Launch of IRS-P2
C. Launch of IRS-1B
D. Launch of IRS-1C
accepted.x: The correct order is IRS-1A (1988), IRS-1B (1991), IRS-1C (1995) and IRS-P2 (1994) — wait, because IRS-P2 was launched in 1994, the actual chronological order is A, C, B, D?
accepted.tq: Order the missions by their stated years, checking the middle events carefully.
accepted.sec: EO satellite series → application; early IRS launch sites  [APPSC]
